newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Anglo Irish Bank dismisses takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: Anglo Irish Bank dismisses takeover talk.

text.p: Anglo Irish Bank Corp Plc on Tuesday dismissed recent market speculation that the bank was a likely subject of a takeover bid.
"No-one has spoken to our chairman or myself either formally or informally," chief executive Sean Fitzpatrick told a news conference after the bank published full-year results.
Earlier, the bank posted a 26-percent increase in pre-tax profit to 24.1 million Irish pounds while earnings per share (EPS) rose by 31 percent to 7.46 Irish pence.
Fitzpatrick said the bank had increased its share in the middle market to 10 percent where it now has a clear franchise.
The bank's average loan size is around half a million Irish pounds and it is involved in lending to areas such as investment property, the pub and hotel sector and the professional sector.

Fitzpatrick said the bank would like to see compound growth of around 15 percent in net lending and deposits in the next few years and would also keep an eye out for suitable acquisitions in Britain and Ireland.
